research.job_description_summary: Zoho hires freshers in India as Software Developers. A May 2026 FACE Prep guide and 2026 Glassdoor reviews describe a written round (aptitude plus programming and output questions, offline), basic and advanced programming rounds, a low-level design or data-modeling round that varies by hiring team, a technical HR round that starts with the candidate's project, and a general HR round. The guide notes the sequence varies by drive and that Zoho's careers page is the primary reference; that page was not fetched.
required_skills: C or C++ programming and output prediction
limitations: Zoho's official careers page was not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED.

The FACE Prep guide (2026-05-07) labels its sample questions as examples, not verbatim reports; they are used as topic context (class D). Its claims of 'reported candidate experiences' are not attributed to named sources.

Candidate-attributed material is four Glassdoor reviews (Software Developer and Software Engineer, February to August 2026): the written round had about 10 aptitude and 10 programming questions; one reviewer was asked to optimise code; another got a stock management data modeling question. Those topics are class B, one report each, with the actual problems rewritten.
One review mentions Java and another C++ for the same round, so the written-round language is uncertain.
Zoho runs pen-and-paper rounds; the coding items here assume a normal editor and test cases.
Round order and skipped rounds vary by drive.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.
Source pages on LeetCode Discuss and Glassdoor returned HTTP 403 to the CodeArena audit tool (2026-10-11), so the cited questions were not re-confirmed against those pages.
